overall: On reconsideration, the AG reissued OML 2024-7 and found no Open Meeting Law violation on any allegation, reversing the earlier finding that the April 22, 2023 executive session lacked a lawful purpose.

allegations.summary: A member of the public was kept out of the meeting room for several minutes after a quorum arrived, and the commissioners reportedly discussed unrelated matters meanwhile.
allegations.key_passage: We find that any brief discussions that took place once a quorum was reached but before the complainant was granted entry into the meeting room were limited to social pleasantries and the like and did not constitute discussion of matters within the Commission’s jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: The Commission allegedly called police to maintain order and keep the complainant out of the April 22 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Here, where police were specifically asked only to be present if needed to maintain order and to ensure only authorized individuals attended the executive session, and police did not even arrive until after the complainant had voluntarily left the meeting once the executive session began, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The Commission allegedly convened in executive session on April 22 to discuss purchasing farmland under Purpose 6 without a lawful purpose, after a notice citing a repealed statute.
allegations.key_passage: we are satisfied that the Commission has demonstrated that in these circumstances, an open meeting may have a detrimental effect on the negotiating position of the public body.

allegations.summary: Non-member attendees (an advisor who lives outside town and a commissioner's adult son) were allowed in the meeting room and executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We find no error with the Commission’s decision to allow these two individuals to be present prior to the start of the meeting and note that had the executive session been convened for a proper purpose, these individuals’ presence in the executive session would have been permissible then as well.
